$comment: SECOND bps_conversion CONFORMANCE VECTOR (issue #823). The corpus in consensus-receipt.assembler-input.json / consensus-receipt.valid.json has a whole-basis-point mean — raw = [1250, 6000, 1750, 1000] — so every remainder is exactly 0, leftover is 0, and neither the apportionment loop nor the tie-break ever executes. That golden therefore cannot discriminate LARGEST REMAINDER from the SUPERSEDED settle-the-last rule: a reimplementation that still does settle-the-last reproduces it byte for byte. This vector has a nonzero leftover AND an exact three-way tie, so the two rules disagree on it — 'produces expected_weight_bps.weights' is a real conformance check here, not a vacuous one.

expected_weight_bps.rule: LARGEST REMAINDER (Hare quota), tie broken by canonical_bucket_order — the rule schema 1.0 implements. See bps_conversion in consensus-receipt.canonicalization.json, and bucketSharesToBps() in contract/src/consensus-receipt.js.

discriminates_from.rule: the SUPERSEDED rule (bps_conversion.superseded_rule): round the first three canonical buckets to the nearest bp, then settle the positionally last bucket to 10000 minus their sum. Committed here so a reimplementation that still does this, rather than largest remainder, is caught by a byte/vector mismatch against expected_weight_bps rather than passing silently.

why_this_vector: Every share is exactly 1/3 except real_world_assets, which is exactly 0. floor(1/3 * 10000) = 3333 for each of the first three buckets, leaving a leftover of 1 bp; all three carry the IDENTICAL binary64 remainder (0.3333333333333333 * 10000 - 3333 is bitwise equal three times over), so this is a genuine tie and canonical_bucket_order decides it — agent_tokens, the earliest of the three tied buckets, takes the leftover bp. Under the superseded rule the same vector rounds each of the first three to the nearest bp (3333 each, prefix 9999) and settles real_world_assets — the bucket the committee allocated NOTHING to — to 10000 - 9999 = 1 bp: the exact defect issue #798/robotmoney-core#1290 removed the rule for, reproduced here as a byte-level discriminator rather than only as a corpus statistic.
reference: bucketSharesToBps() in contract/src/consensus-receipt.js is the reference implementation. consensus-receipt-bps-conversion.test.ts's 'an exact tie is broken by canonical bucket order' test exercises this exact share vector under the name 'thirds'; this file publishes it as a standalone cross-repo conformance vector rather than only an in-repo assertion.
